item.title: ‘It Takes Two’ Rapper Rob Base Dead at 59
item.description:
[Energetic music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: "Welcome to our show, where we dive into the world of music and entertainment. Today, we're taking a moment to remember a hip-hop legend who left us far too soon. Rob Base, one half of the iconic duo Rob Base & DJ E-Z Rock, passed away on Friday, May 22nd, just days after celebrating his 59th birthday.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: "According to his family, Rob Base died peacefully, surrounded by loved ones, after a private battle with cancer. The Harlem native, born Robert Ginyard, made a lasting impact on the music industry with his unique energy and creativity.
[Clip of "It Takes Two" plays briefly]
Host: "You might know him best for the hit single 'It Takes Two', which peaked at number 36 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and spent 16 weeks on the chart. The song, released in 1988, was a game-changer for the duo and paved the way for their success.
[Music transitions to a montage of Rob Base's other hits]
Host: "Rob Base and DJ E-Z Rock went on to release several other hits, including 'Get on the Dance Floor' and 'Joy and Pain'. They also dropped two albums together, 'It Takes Two' and 'Break of Dawn', and Rob Base even released a solo album, 'The Incredible Base'.
[Clip of "Rock That Body" by The Black Eyed Peas plays briefly]
Host: "Rob Base's music has been sampled and featured in numerous films, TV shows, and video games, including 'Love & Basketball', 'The Proposal', and 'Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas'. The Black Eyed Peas even sampled 'It Takes Two' in their hit single 'Rock That Body'.
[Music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: "Rob Base's legacy extends beyond his music. He was a loving father, family man, and friend, and his impact will never be forgotten. He even ventured into Hollywood, executive producing the horror movie 'Urban Flesh Eaters' in 2025.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: "Rob Base's final public statement was just earlier this week, when he celebrated his 59th birthday on Instagram. He wrote, 'Happy 59th Birthday to me. God thank you for allowing me to see another year.' It's a poignant reminder to appreciate the time we have and the memories we create.
[Music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: "We'll miss Rob Base, but his music and legacy will live on. Rest in peace, Rob Base. May 18, 1967 – May 22, 2026."
[Music fades out, and the host's voice takes over for a final time]
Host: "Thanks for tuning in to our show. Join us next time as we explore more stories from the world of music and entertainment."
